body:
pep-435 is ambiguous about iterating over enums, with just the phrase "Within an enumeration, the values can be compared by identity, and the enumeration itself can be iterated over." being all it has.  It does however fully define `__members__` and that's also [what we document](https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/14/core/type_basics.html?highlight=enum#sqlalchemy.types.Enum) as well as use in tests.

So it has to keep using `__members__` but it can just use a `set()` to check for dupes.

If you intend to keep using `__members__`, the docs define how to get aliases here:
https://docs.python.org/3/library/enum.html#iteration

So you can replace `!=` with `==` to get the actual enum names:

```[name for name, member in Shape.__members__.items() if member.name == name]```


EDIT: Now I see, you need to be compatible with pep-435 that can allow anything, so yes, you need to use a set
EDIT 2: No, enums must have `.name`, so you can use that and also a set might pick an alias instead of the original name (Python < 3.6, I guess). Specially because pep-435 uses that same line to define how to find aliases

@zzzeek While this may be a 1.3 backport, I think we could limit to 1.4 since it would change the behaviour.

We currently have tests that ensure the current handling of alias values, so if we want to change it I think it could be for 1.4 only.

**Federico Caselli** has proposed a fix for this issue in the **master** branch:

**Correctly handle aliases in :class:`_sql.Enum`** https://gerrit.sqlalchemy.org/c/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/+/2686

I'm pretty sure we write the names of the enums, not the values to the db. So "four" is written in the db:

```
psycopg2.errors.InvalidTextRepresentation: invalid input value for enum someenum: "four"
LINE 1: ...3, 'one'),(4, 'three'),(5, 'three'),(6, 'three'),(7, 'four')
```

ohhh... right we do write the names , just re-read the top of the post.    

well then this is a huge backwards-incompatible thing.   not really sure what to do besides adding an ugly flag.   someone that already has aliases on their enums already has those values in their DB.
i think "omit_aliases=True" flag that does the "name == self.name" behavior is the only way to go here.

Great label the "quagmire" one :)

I think we could place that flag to False in 1.4, and use deprecation 2.0 here to turn that True by default in 2.0

I think you could show a warning if the enum has aliases and the user didn't pick the flag value.

But i don't believe someone would want aliases stored. Because you will fragment the data. If they want to rename the enum value stored, they can do a migration

> But i don't believe someone would want aliases stored. Because you will fragment the data. If they want to rename the enum value stored, they can do a migration

that's not as easy as it should be. For example, when using postgresql native enums, there is no way of removing enum values, you can only add them to an enum type.

So sadly I think it we will need to keep this flag for the foreseeable future. But yes, I think we will have a warning shown if the enum has aliases and the flag is not specified. Probably the flag will be initially off, and we could probably toggle it to on in v2
